title: Free: The Future Of A Radical Price

questions.q: Where does the summary trace the phrase about there being no free lunch?
a: Saloons serving salty food to sell more drinks
Hotels offering meals to attract travelers
Bakers giving away scraps to the poor
Railroads including meals in every ticket
questions.why: The first lesson explains that salty free food made cowboys thirsty, so they bought beer.

questions.q: How was free mainly used before the internet, according to the summary?
a: To make you pay for something else
To reward only the most loyal customers
To clear out unwanted old inventory
To avoid government price rules
questions.why: The first lesson compares free razors, phones and magazines that all required a later purchase.

questions.q: How is value measured in the online gift economy?
a: By the attention people give you
By the price you are able to charge
By the size of your company
By the speed of your website
questions.why: The second lesson says a post nobody reads has no value, so attention replaces money as the measure.

a: Giving the basic product away and charging for extras
Charging everyone a small monthly fee
Offering discounts once a trial period ends
Selling ads inside a paid product
questions.why: The third lesson defines it as free basics plus paid features, services and related products.

questions.q: What should you do once a free product has built an audience?
a: Find out what they want and charge for that
Raise the price of everything you already make
Stop publishing and sell your contact list
Copy whatever bigger competitors charge
questions.why: The third lesson says free work wins attention, and attention is what you later convert into sales.
